item.title: The sacred testimony of Black joy
item.description: As we mark Black History Month—100 years after Carter G. Woodson inaugurated Black History Week in 1926, and as the organization he founded reflects on a century of commemorating Black life—I find myself thinking about Black joy.

item.title: Facebook group helps women find healing after alleged abuse at Baptist counseling facility
item.description: More than 100 women have found refuge in an online support group that exists because of trauma they say they experienced at a place meant to heal them.

item.title: New PBS docuseries examines the interwoven history of Black and Jewish Americans
item.description: A new four-part PBS documentary series traces the history between Black and Jewish Americans, examining their connection through shared experiences of persecution and how they’ve navigated political tests to the relationship.

item.title: Morality requires other people
item.description: In a New Yorker cartoon, two self-contented businessmen relax in wingback chairs. One says to the other: “I, too, longed to find a cause greater than myself. Fortunately, I never did.”

item.title: St Peter Returns to the Garden
item.description: God of calloused hands, and splinters,and wooden bowls full of dinner,I returned here with morning,wanting to return to that last eveningwe spent together, all of usin a shadowed room,our sorrow true as winter.

item.title: For 2026 Super Bowl He Gets Us ad goes more personal less political
item.description: Back in 2021, a group of evangelical families, including the founders of Hobby Lobby, began funding a new ad campaign in the United States, hoping to help skeptics give Jesus a second look and to convince people to be a little kinder to one another.
